summary: Read a 32-bit integer and reverse the order of its bits. The old low bit becomes the high bit. Keep the width at 32, filling open places with 0, and write the integer named by the reversed bits. In languages without an unsigned type, both the value you read and the value you write are signed, but you still reverse that same bit pattern. Under two's complement, reading -3 must write -1073741825. Do not alter the reversal because a sign bit is set.
notes: Compare after trimming trailing newlines. The input is tokens in the same order as the method parameters.
